observational_test.interpretation: Under both nuisance treatments the SPARC rotation curves require mass beyond the observed baryons, so option 2 is falsified for disc galaxies. This falsifies one assistant-proposed operationalization only. Option 1 is untestable and option 3 is untested. Calling the missing mass 'emergent matter' would be a relabelling unless Candidate A independently predicted its amount and distribution.

policy: Both A and B are selected research candidates, run concurrently as separate programs with separate preregistrations and artifacts. Evidence about one is not evidence for the other without a frozen comparison. Keep recovered intent, standard physics, restricted test hypotheses and empirical evidence separate. Selection is not physical validation.

selected_restricted_test.kappa_lo_meaning: lowest k for which (k, k) lies inside the published observed 95% joint region; the SM point (1, 1) is inside
flags_raised: every m5 = 1200 GeV point exceeds the |mu5/sqrt(Lambda)| < 1 convention at mu4_max; at R^-1 = 10 and 100 GeV it also exceeds lambda0 <= 1
R^-1 = 1000 GeV with m5 = 600 and 1200 GeV give a lightest-additional-state lower-bound width above 1% of its mass at mu4_max
selected_restricted_test.higgs_mass_sensitivity: M_H = 125.2 GeV changes mu4_max by at most 0.4%
selected_restricted_test.interpretation: The restricted hypothesis predicts kappa_V = kappa_F = kappa <= 1 and therefore contains the SM decoupling limit, so this data set can bound mu4 but cannot refute the restricted model. The result is conditional compatibility, not evidence for Candidate B.

test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.data_product: ATLAS Nature 607 (2022) 52, HEPData ins2104706 v1, observed -2 ln Lambda(mu) for the global signal strength with all systematics
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.interval_kind: asymptotic one-sided 95% CL lower limit on mu = kappa^2 at fixed (R, m5, Lambda); not a joint interval over the grid
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.comparison_with_contour: weaker than the first-test contour bound at every grid point, so the contour remains the stronger Higgs-rate bound

test_b_cms_direct_resonance.data_product: CMS-HIG-24-002, HEPData ins3161000 v1, observed and expected 95% CL upper limits on sigma x BR(X -> ZZ) for ggF and VBF with NWA, 1, 10 and 100 GeV width hypotheses
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.not_covered_reason: at m5 = 1200 GeV every heavy state lies above the 1 TeV tabulated theory range; the labelled extrapolated variant excludes nothing
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.heuristic_tower_clusters: a heuristic comparison of summed nearby tower states exceeds a CMS limit below the Higgs-rate bound at 7 grid points, including R^-1 = 10 GeV; it is labelled heuristic and is not the result

selected_extended_tests.combined_statement: per grid point the reported bound is min(contour, likelihood, CMS); an intersection of separate 95% CL-type constraints, not a joint statistical combination
caveats: interference with the gg -> ZZ continuum, the off-shell 125 GeV tail and among nearby tower states is neglected
each production mode is compared alone
signal acceptance and shapes are assumed to match the CMS SM-like scalar hypothesis
heavy-state scalar widths are tree level; SM-like widths above 1 TeV are extrapolated
asymptotic likelihood statistics; no toy calibration
selected_extended_tests.interpretation: mu4 = 0 is the SM limit and is always allowed, so both tests bound the restricted coupling and cannot refute the restricted family. The CMS search is the stronger bound at 3 of 12 grid points. Neither result is evidence for Candidate B.
deferred: signal-background interference and joint ggF + VBF treatment
a direct-resonance likelihood from a published statistical model
